stem: Dev bubbles his exhaled air through lime water in one tube. Fresh air from outside is bubbled through lime water in a second tube. Only the exhaled-air tube turns milky. Both tubes start with clear lime water.

options.text: Exhaled air has more carbon dioxide than the fresh air tested, but exhaled air still contains some oxygen.
Lime water turning milky shows that oxygen increased in the exhaled-air tube.
Exhaled air contains no oxygen at all.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Lime water turns milky with carbon dioxide, so exhaled air has more CO2 than fresh air; not all inhaled oxygen is used up, so exhaled air still contains some oxygen.

teacher.key_rationale: Milky lime water marks carbon dioxide, so exhaled air has more CO2 than fresh air. Exhaled air still contains oxygen; milky lime water does not prove oxygen increased.
